segments.speaker: Cold Open
segments.text: We just want to give tools to the whole scientific community.
segments.translation: 我们只是想为整个科学界提供工具。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We want to understand how biology works.
segments.translation: 我们想了解生物学是如何运作的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I want to understand the genetics of this person.
segments.translation: 我想了解这个人的遗传学。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I want to understand the risks they have to different illnesses.
segments.translation: 我想了解他们对不同疾病的风险。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: My goal is to be able to treat the individual as an individual, understand the mechanisms and be able to intervene.
segments.translation: 我的目标是能够将个体作为个体来对待，理解其机制并能够进行干预。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We'll have a bigger impact by getting this and more scientists hands quicker by doing it as open source projects instead.
segments.translation: 通过将这些工具以开源项目的形式更快地交到更多科学家手中，我们将产生更大的影响。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's not just like there's some factory somewhere that you can pay to produce the data you actually need to invent new novel scientific approaches.
segments.translation: 这不像某个地方有工厂，你可以花钱生产数据，你实际上需要发明新的科学方法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The theory isn't that we're going to cure the diseases.
segments.translation: 我们的理论不是我们要治愈疾病。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We're not.
segments.translation: 我们不会。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's that we want to help accelerate the pace of progress for the whole scientific field.
segments.translation: 而是我们希望帮助加速整个科学领域的进步步伐。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We folded over 1.1 billion proteins and predicted their structures, and we didn't design A model for antibodies, we didn't design A model to be able to bind one particular target.
segments.translation: 我们折叠了超过11亿个蛋白质并预测了它们的结构，我们没有为抗体设计模型，也没有设计一个能够结合特定靶点的模型。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We just designed a model that could understand proteins.
segments.translation: 我们只是设计了一个能够理解蛋白质的模型。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: If we could design A protein to actually change the Physiology, then we can actually cure someone.
segments.translation: 如果我们能设计出一种蛋白质来真正改变生理机能，那么我们就能真正治愈某人。

segments.speaker: Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan, and Alex Rives Introduction
segments.text: Today on No Priors, we're joined by Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan, and Alex Reeves.
segments.translation: 今天的“无先验”节目，我们邀请了马克·扎克伯格、普莉希拉·陈和亚历克斯·里夫斯。

segments.speaker: Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan, and Alex Rives Introduction
segments.text: We'll be talking about Biohub and all their various efforts to now start applying AI at scale to do world models of cells and different levels of interactions across biology.
segments.translation: 我们将讨论Biohub以及他们目前将人工智能大规模应用于细胞世界模型和生物学不同层面相互作用的各种努力。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Mark Priscilla, thank you for doing this.
segments.translation: 马克、普莉希拉，谢谢你们做这些。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for having.
segments.translation: 是的，谢谢邀请。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: US here.
segments.translation: 我们来这里。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Alex, congratulations on new missions.
segments.translation: 亚历克斯，祝贺你承担新任务。

segments.speaker: Why Biohub and Their Mission
segments.text: Thank you.
segments.translation: 谢谢。

segments.speaker: Why Biohub and Their Mission
segments.text: You guys made Biohub your primary philanthropic effort and then committed $500 million to this virtual biology initiative.
segments.translation: 你们将Biohub作为主要的慈善事业，并承诺向这个虚拟生物学计划投入5亿美元。

segments.speaker: Why Biohub and Their Mission
segments.text: Can you tell us a little bit about, you know, why do that and how did you go from we should fund this to this is like who we are?
segments.translation: 你们能告诉我们一些关于为什么这样做，以及你们是如何从“我们应该资助这个”发展到“这就是我们”的吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So Biohub in its current form, we're super excited about.
segments.translation: 所以，我们对Biohub目前的形态感到非常兴奋。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We feel like it's a really good fit for who we are and what we bring to the table and what we can achieve together.
segments.translation: 我们觉得它非常适合我们的身份、我们能带来的东西以及我们能共同实现的目标。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But this work started 10 years ago when we were thinking about how can we give back.
segments.translation: 但这项工作始于十年前，当时我们正在思考如何回馈社会。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And Mark had.
segments.translation: 马克曾。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Mark wanted to build an organization that could cure, prevent and manage all disease by the end of the century.
segments.translation: 马克想建立一个组织，到本世纪末能够治愈、预防和管理所有疾病。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And we had a series of hilarious meetings with scientists that, like famous Nobel Prize winning scientists, were just laughing at us.
segments.translation: 我们和科学家们开了一系列搞笑的会议，那些著名的诺贝尔奖得主科学家们只是在嘲笑我们。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Is that was that your starting line?
segments.translation: 那是你的起点吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: We're just going to cure all the disease.
segments.translation: 我们就是要治愈所有疾病。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: No, no.
segments.translation: 不，不。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And to be clear, we don't think that we're going to be the ones curing the diseases.
segments.translation: 需要明确的是，我们不认为我们会是治愈疾病的人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Our our goal was always to build tools that could accelerate the whole scientific fields.
segments.translation: 我们的目标始终是构建能够加速整个科学领域的工具。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That way the scientific field collectively could cure all the diseases.
segments.translation: 这样，科学界就能共同治愈所有疾病。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But still, I think people thought that by the end of the century was a stretch.
segments.translation: 但即便如此，我想人们还是觉得“到本世纪末”有点夸张。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now I think it's like too conservative.
segments.translation: 现在我觉得这太保守了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so we're kept being like, OK, well, we have these series of funny, awkward educational conversations where we're like, OK, but like, why?
segments.translation: 所以我们一直在想，好吧，我们进行了一系列有趣、尴尬的教育性对话，我们问：好吧，但是为什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Like, why do you think it's impossible?
segments.translation: 你为什么认为这不可能？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And like, you know, just being the the person in the room was just like, oh, I don't know why You tell me.
segments.translation: 你知道，就像房间里那个人一样，只是说：哦，我不知道，你告诉我。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Finally, we got people to like, they're like, fine, if you really must know.
segments.translation: 最后，我们让人们说：好吧，如果你真的想知道的话。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And we're like, you know, we do.
segments.translation: 我们说，你知道，我们确实想知道。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It seems important.
segments.translation: 这似乎很重要。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's, you know, they were like, well, we work in silos and when you publish information doesn't get shared, it gets locked up for long periods of time and we don't have tooling.
segments.translation: 他们说，嗯，我们各自为政，当你发布信息时，它不会被分享，会被长期锁定，而且我们没有工具。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You know, they gave the example of like we build a great tool by 1 postdoc in the lab and it lives on their computer.
segments.translation: 你知道，他们举例说，我们实验室里的一名博士后开发了一个很棒的工具，它就存在于他的电脑上。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And when they graduate, the tool is gone.
segments.translation: 当他们毕业时，这个工具就消失了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And they just, it was what we heard was very hard to build shared tools to move science faster, build the shared knowledge base to quickly move science faster.
segments.translation: 他们只是，我们听到的是，很难建立共享工具来加速科学发展，也很难建立共享知识库来快速加速科学发展。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And that's sort of where we began and thinking about, OK, like if those are the problems, like what can we contribute?
segments.translation: 这就是我们开始思考的地方：好吧，如果这些是问题，我们能贡献什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yeah, I mean, so the original Biohub model was basically focus on long term tool development by bringing together engineers and scientists across multiple universities to focus on long term tool development.
segments.translation: 是的，我的意思是，最初的Biohub模式基本上是专注于长期工具开发，通过汇集多所大学的工程师和科学家来专注于长期工具开发。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And it basically it, it like worked.
segments.translation: 它基本上，它就像奏效了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And you know, we started off with with CCI doing a number of different things.
segments.translation: 你知道，我们最初与CCI合作做了许多不同的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And I think over time we just felt like, OK, the science piece is really working.
segments.translation: 我认为随着时间的推移，我们只是觉得，好吧，科学部分确实在发挥作用。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And we just kept on investing more and more and more in it until now it is basically the primary and main thing that we're doing.
segments.translation: 我们只是不断地投入越来越多，直到现在它基本上是我们正在做的主要和核心的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And we've expanded the original San Francisco Biohub to a handful now at this point.
segments.translation: 我们已经将最初的旧金山Biohub扩展到目前为止的几个。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: There's New York, there's Chicago.
segments.translation: 有纽约，有芝加哥。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The real focus in the unifying theme at this point is, is the virtual biology initiative around taking the unique data sets that are able to be generated in order to model effectively, starting with the smallest pieces of of proteins, but then eventually cells and whole biological systems.
segments.translation: 目前真正的重点和统一主题是围绕虚拟生物学倡议，利用能够生成的独特数据集，有效地建模，从最小的蛋白质片段开始，但最终是细胞和整个生物系统。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But that's kind of how how we've evolved is, you know, this, this idea that that we talked about around that some of this is an AI problem and you want to build a frontier AI lab.
segments.translation: 但这大概就是我们如何演变而来的，你知道，我们讨论过的这个想法，其中一些是人工智能问题，你想建立一个前沿人工智能实验室。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But you need to couple that with a frontier biology effort that can do the work of, of, of basically being able to understand and get the data that you need to actually be able to build these models.
segments.translation: 但你需要将其与前沿生物学努力相结合，后者能够完成理解和获取实际构建这些模型所需数据的工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Because unlike language models, there's just like a lot of data out there on the Internet.
segments.translation: 因为不像语言模型，互联网上有很多数据。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That's not really the case with biology.
segments.translation: 生物学的情况并非如此。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I mean, there are obviously a bunch of different data sets that exist that academia and scientists have generated over the the decades.
segments.translation: 我的意思是，当然存在许多不同的数据集，这些数据集是学术界和科学家们几十年来生成的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But a lot of the stuff that I think we want to put into this, it doesn't exist, right?
segments.translation: 但我们想投入的很多东西，我认为它并不存在，对吧？

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's like you want to go to visualize things that people haven't been able to see before, which is why we're doing the the imaging work.
segments.translation: 就像你想去可视化人们以前从未见过的事物，这就是我们正在进行成像工作的原因。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You want to be able to record things that are going on inside the body, which is why we're doing the kind of cellular engineering work.
segments.translation: 你希望能够记录身体内部发生的事情，这就是我们正在进行细胞工程工作的原因。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You want to be able to measure things like inflammation in ways that haven't been possible, which is why the, you know, Chicago Biohub is focused on building those kind of devices and being able to do that.
segments.translation: 你希望能够以以前不可能的方式测量炎症等，这就是为什么芝加哥Biohub专注于构建这些设备并能够做到这一点。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And that will fundamentally create new types of data sets that will allow new types of models.
segments.translation: 这将从根本上创造新型数据集，从而允许新型模型。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And I think it's just a very exciting thing that I'm going back to what you're saying if the if the scientific field, it primarily needs kind of tool development that now is going to empower scientists across the the field to be able to do their work faster.
segments.translation: 我认为这是一件非常令人兴奋的事情，回到你所说的，如果科学领域主要需要工具开发，那么现在这将赋能整个领域的科学家更快地完成他们的工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That's what we think we can provide through this kind of long term focus on tool development.
segments.translation: 这就是我们认为我们可以通过这种长期专注于工具开发来提供的东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But the I think there's a fun through line on where we started and you know, bringing us to our work to with that Alex is driving now is that our very first request for application RFA here was around single cell sequencing.
segments.translation: 但是，我认为我们从哪里开始，以及现在亚历克斯正在推动的工作之间，有一条有趣的线索，那就是我们在这里的第一个申请请求（RFA）是关于单细胞测序的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And we wanted to look at sort of like the RNA that is transcribed in individual cells and that bought that was possible, but it was still pretty early on in understanding how different cells were expressing their DNA to the point where at the beginning we were just funding methods like getting people to describe how to do it so that others could share that methodology.
segments.translation: 我们想研究单个细胞中转录的RNA，这在当时是可能的，但对于理解不同细胞如何表达其DNA来说，还处于早期阶段，以至于一开始我们只是资助方法，让人们描述如何做，以便其他人可以分享这种方法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And then that became us funding the Human Cell Atlas, which is now one of the largest databases of single cell transcriptomes.
segments.translation: 然后这变成了我们资助人类细胞图谱，它现在是最大的单细胞转录组数据库之一。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It was getting hard for scientists to annotate the data.
segments.translation: 科学家们发现注释数据变得困难。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So we built Cell by Gene, which was like a very simple annotation tool that scientists could use to make use of that data.
segments.translation: 所以我们构建了Cell by Gene，这是一个非常简单的注释工具，科学家们可以用它来利用这些数据。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Then the community came around Cell by Gene, built around Cell by Gene, and started contributing more and more data that we had nothing to do with sort of creating or funding or making happen in the world.
segments.translation: 然后社区围绕Cell by Gene建立起来，并开始贡献越来越多的数据，而这些数据的创建、资助或实现与我们无关。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And now Cell by Gene is a corpus of knowledge that a lot of the transcriptomic based models are based off of and is used regularly by the scientific community.
segments.translation: 现在，Cell by Gene是一个知识库，许多基于转录组的模型都以此为基础，并被科学界定期使用。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But still, there are always critiques like this is just stamp collecting, like you're just gathering bits of knowledge, sorry, bits of data.
segments.translation: 但仍然总有批评，比如这只是收集邮票，你只是收集零碎的知识，抱歉，零碎的数据。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And we're not going to be able to pull scientific knowledge and wisdom and insights out of and and we're like, well, we didn't have an answer for a while.
segments.translation: 我们无法从中提取科学知识、智慧和见解，我们当时对此无言以对。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And then imagine our delight when large language models became a huge topic of conversation that could make sense of large amounts of data.
segments.translation: 然后，当大型语言模型成为一个热门话题，能够理解大量数据时，想象一下我们的喜悦。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And I just for me is like, what if we could actually understand how biology worked?
segments.translation: 对我来说，这就像，如果我们真的能理解生物学是如何运作的呢？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Move it from a discovery based science to an engineering based science where we could systematically understand how living beings, living cells worked and be able to understand why things go wrong.
segments.translation: 将其从基于发现的科学转变为基于工程的科学，我们可以系统地理解生物、活细胞是如何运作的，并能够理解为什么会出现问题。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so when we saw that moment, we're like, this is it something really big could happen here?
segments.translation: 所以当我们看到那一刻，我们想，就是它了，这里可能会发生一些非常大的事情。

segments.speaker: Integrating Frontier AI and Frontier Biology
segments.text: Alex, you were you started at Metafair, but you were on the path to, you know, you'd assemble the team in evolutionary scale and you'd raise venture and you were making progress in your models.
segments.translation: 亚历克斯，你最初在Metafair工作，但你正在朝着组建进化规模团队、筹集风险投资并在模型方面取得进展的道路前进。

segments.speaker: Integrating Frontier AI and Frontier Biology
segments.text: What was the pitch from Mark and Priscilla where you said like, that's actually the right way to go after the mission?
segments.translation: 马克和普莉希拉的提议是什么，让你觉得那才是实现使命的正确途径？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Well, I think for me, it was really kind of the moment when I understood that, you know, they, they really saw this as as an integration of frontier AI and frontier biology.
segments.translation: 嗯，我想对我来说，真正重要的是我明白了，你知道，他们确实将这视为前沿人工智能和前沿生物学的整合。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And I think I had developed conviction that, you know, this is really a, a new era of science that's, that's just beginning kind of what's going to be possible with artificial intelligence.
segments.translation: 我认为我已经确信，你知道，这确实是一个新的科学时代，它才刚刚开始，人工智能将带来什么可能性。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And, you know, we're, we're in the age of information theory at scale.
segments.translation: 你知道，我们正处于大规模信息论的时代。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And we have these systems that can basically kind of predict the next token.
segments.translation: 我们有这些系统，它们基本上可以预测下一个标记。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And they can, you know, learn world models from that.
segments.translation: 它们可以，你知道，从中学习世界模型。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: They can learn biology from the data.
segments.translation: 它们可以从数据中学习生物学。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And so, you know, I, I think that it just, it was really clear that, you know, to build kind of that next, that next kind of institution for the next era, you would really need to have frontier artificial intelligence.
segments.translation: 所以，你知道，我认为很清楚，要建立下一个时代的下一个机构，你确实需要拥有前沿人工智能。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: You would have to have frontier biology.
segments.translation: 你必须拥有前沿生物学。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: You would need to start to put those things and feedback and really have models that are learning from the biology.
segments.translation: 你需要开始将这些东西结合起来并进行反馈，真正拥有从生物学中学习的模型。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And I think, you know, it's just, and you need the right scale and the right people.
segments.translation: 我认为，你知道，你还需要合适的规模和合适的人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And so this, this just really felt, I think like the way to do that.
segments.translation: 所以这，这真的让我觉得是实现这一目标的方式。

segments.speaker: Micro to Macro Biological Modeling
segments.text: There's a variety of different models that you all have been working on.
segments.translation: 你们一直在研究各种不同的模型。

segments.speaker: Micro to Macro Biological Modeling
segments.text: And I think it's kind of interesting because some of the earliest breakthroughs in biology were things like alpha fold where, you know, there's a Google model that showed that you could do protein folding at scale in a really interesting way that people didn't realize was very tractable.
segments.translation: 我认为这很有趣，因为生物学领域最早的一些突破是像AlphaFold这样的东西，你知道，谷歌的模型展示了你可以以一种非常有趣的方式大规模进行蛋白质折叠，而人们以前没有意识到这是非常可行的。

segments.speaker: Micro to Macro Biological Modeling

segments.translation: 我认为这只是我们正在做的事情的雄心壮志，以及我们承诺做这件事的时间跨度。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I think part of the theory is like if you're building tools that are this complicated, you kind of want to have a 10 to 15 year time horizon on, on building out these efforts.
segments.translation: 我认为理论的一部分是，如果你正在构建如此复杂的工具，你希望有10到15年的时间跨度来构建这些努力。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And then the scale of capital required.
segments.translation: 然后是所需的资本规模。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I mean, I guess there's no rule that said that you couldn't do it as like an incredibly well funded startup.
segments.translation: 我的意思是，我想没有规定说你不能把它做成一个资金极其充足的初创公司。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But I think that this just made more sense.
segments.translation: 但我认为这更有意义。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And then it also is, is simplifying strategically to not have to think about how you're going to make money with the different things.
segments.translation: 然后它在战略上也简化了，不必考虑如何用不同的东西赚钱。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And we just, we want to get the models in people's hands.
segments.translation: 我们只是，我们想把模型交到人们手中。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We release them as open source.
segments.translation: 我们将其作为开源发布。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I think that that's like a very valuable thing to do.
segments.translation: 我认为这是一件非常有价值的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And again, I mean, the, the, the theory isn't that we're going to cure the diseases, We're not.
segments.translation: 再说一遍，我的意思是，理论上我们不会治愈这些疾病，我们不会。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's that we want to help accelerate the pace of progress for the whole scientific field.
segments.translation: 我们是想帮助加速整个科学领域的进步步伐。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: As the person least experienced with making money here, I would say that there you the sort of neutral, non profit nature of our work actually helps harness more people to enter this effort.
segments.translation: 作为这里赚钱经验最少的人，我想说，我们工作的这种中立、非营利性质实际上有助于吸引更多人参与这项工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And to actually achieve the mission of like understanding the totality of human biology and to cure, prevent, manage all disease, you actually do need the entire academic biotech industry to come together and to work on this in a sort of unified way.
segments.translation: 要真正实现理解人类生物学全貌、治愈、预防和管理所有疾病的使命，你确实需要整个学术界、生物技术产业齐心协力，以一种统一的方式来开展这项工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: In part because there's a lot of talent out there.
segments.translation: 部分原因是外面有很多优秀人才。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And it's, it's not helpful to leave any talent, exclude any talent from the effort.
segments.translation: 而且，不让任何人才参与，将任何人才排除在外，都是没有帮助的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And there's a super long tail of diseases.
segments.translation: 而且疾病种类繁多。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There are the common ones and even the common ones, I think if you unbundle heart disease, cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, even if you unbundle like dementia or depression, there are many, many, many subcategories that become more and more niche.
segments.translation: 有常见的疾病，即使是常见的疾病，我认为如果你把心脏病、癌症、神经退行性疾病，甚至痴呆症或抑郁症拆分开来，它们也有许多许多子类别，变得越来越小众。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And that's not even looking at the long, long tail of rare diseases.
segments.translation: 这甚至还没有考虑到罕见病的漫长尾部。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Those often get orphaned and don't get brought along when we're sort of looking at what the most efficient way to impact the lives of many.
segments.translation: 当我们考虑如何最有效地影响许多人的生活时，这些疾病常常被遗弃，没有得到关注。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But if you've sort of decentralized the effort and put the tools in many people's hands, you start getting people who are like, you know what?
segments.translation: 但是，如果你将这项工作分散化，将工具交到许多人手中，你就会开始遇到这样的人，他们会说，你知道吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I am super interested in spinal mass muscular atrophy, and that's something I care deeply about.
segments.translation: 我对脊髓性肌萎缩症非常感兴趣，这是我非常关心的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And if you put the tools in that person's hands, they're going to be able to make progress in a way.
segments.translation: 如果你把工具交到那个人手中，他们就能以某种方式取得进展。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: If you had to focus your efforts and make big bets, you probably wouldn't because it's just a niche, individual, small group disease that actually will.
segments.translation: 如果你必须集中精力进行重大押注，你可能不会这样做，因为它只是一个小众的、个体的、小群体疾病，而它实际上会。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: In turn, if we can understand that disease process helps us unlock knowledge about a lot more about the human how the human body works do.
segments.translation: 反过来，如果我们能理解这种疾病过程，就能帮助我们解锁更多关于人类身体如何运作的知识。

segments.speaker: Understanding How Biology Works
segments.text: You have any thoughts or predictions in terms of what disease areas this work will impact first?
segments.translation: 你对这项工作将首先影响哪些疾病领域有什么想法或预测吗？

segments.speaker: Understanding How Biology Works
segments.text: I know it's very hard to be predictive about these things, but just given the nature of the work and the nature of the models, there are areas you're most optimistic about in the short to medium term.
segments.translation: 我知道预测这些事情很难，但考虑到这项工作的性质和模型的性质，你对短期到中期最乐观的领域有哪些？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I that's actually not how I think about it.
segments.translation: 我其实不是这样想的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: At least the way I think about it is like we want to understand how biology works.
segments.translation: 至少我的想法是，我们想了解生物学是如何运作的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The ideal world is you would say, I understand, I understand the genetics of this person.
segments.translation: 理想的世界是你会说，我理解，我理解这个人的基因。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I want, I want to think about people at the individual level.
segments.translation: 所以我想，我想从个体层面来考虑人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I want to understand the genetics of this person.
segments.translation: 我想了解这个人的基因。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I want to understand the risks they have to different illnesses.
segments.translation: 我想了解他们患不同疾病的风险。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I, I want to understand the mechanistic connection between say a, a gene variant, a protein and a disease process.
segments.translation: 我想了解基因变异、蛋白质和疾病过程之间的机制联系。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Because if you understand that through chain, then you can design A protein, design a drug bespoke to them and actually make an intervention.
segments.translation: 因为如果你理解了这条链，你就可以设计一种蛋白质，设计一种为他们量身定制的药物，并实际进行干预。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And right now, I'm sure we've all had experiences being sick.
segments.translation: 现在，我相信我们都曾生病过。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And if you have something that's even remotely non standard, you go, you go into pub Med, you look up a paper, you look up the supplement and then you start going through the methods and you're like, am I represented in this paper?
segments.translation: 如果你患有某种哪怕是稍微不寻常的疾病，你就会去PubMed，查阅一篇论文，查阅补充材料，然后开始查看方法，你会想，我在这篇论文中被代表了吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And we're just making guesses.
segments.translation: 我们只是在猜测。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We really have no mechanistic understanding.
segments.translation: 我们真的没有机制上的理解。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We're saying like, OK, you're kind of like these people that we studied and this drug kind of impacts the pathway that we think is implicated.
segments.translation: 我们只是说，好吧，你有点像我们研究过的这些人，这种药物似乎影响了我们认为相关的通路。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Let's try and see if anything happens and time passes and sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't.
segments.translation: 让我们试试看是否会发生什么，时间过去了，有时有效，有时无效。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So my goal is to be able to treat the individual as an individual, understand the mechanisms and be able to intervene.
segments.translation: 所以我的目标是能够将个体视为个体来治疗，理解其机制并能够进行干预。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And they're different diseases that are different stages of filling out that whole through line.
segments.translation: 不同的疾病在完成整个过程的不同阶段。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so for some diseases, you just want to understand which gene variants actually cause disease and which don't.
segments.translation: 因此，对于某些疾病，你只想了解哪些基因变异真正导致疾病，哪些不导致。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And that is that in itself can be super empowering to patients.
segments.translation: 这本身就能给患者带来巨大的力量。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And if beyond that, it there's some diseases where we understand the chain, we just can't intervene and change a specific protein function, that's super exciting too.
segments.translation: 如果除此之外，有些疾病我们理解了链条，但我们无法干预并改变特定的蛋白质功能，那也同样令人兴奋。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Like, if we could design A protein to actually change the Physiology, then we can actually cure someone.
segments.translation: 比如，如果我们能设计一种蛋白质来实际改变生理机能，那么我们就能真正治愈某人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But to me, like, that is just as exciting as understanding, contributing to our understanding of, like, how someone gets sick in the first.
segments.translation: 但对我来说，这与理解并促进我们对某人最初如何生病的理解一样令人兴奋。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yeah.
segments.translation: 是的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: That's a very exciting vision because you're basically saying you can bring generalizable tools to provide very personalized things for each individual person, and that's the power of the approaches.
segments.translation: 这是一个非常令人兴奋的愿景，因为你基本上是在说，你可以带来通用的工具，为每个个体提供非常个性化的东西，这就是这些方法的强大之处。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You have these big models that you build that can then apply anywhere.
segments.translation: 你构建了这些大型模型，然后可以应用于任何地方。

segments.speaker: Timeline for Curing All Diseases
segments.text: I know that you mentioned earlier that you were going to try and cure prevent all diseases within 100 years, and you mentioned, hey, it could actually be sooner now given all the advances in AI.
segments.translation: 我知道你之前提到过，你打算在100年内治愈和预防所有疾病，你还提到，鉴于人工智能的所有进步，现在可能更快。

segments.speaker: Timeline for Curing All Diseases
segments.text: Do you have some thought of when we think we'll be closer to that goal?
segments.translation: 你对我们何时能更接近这个目标有什么想法吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Or something.
segments.translation: 或者其他什么。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I mean, I'm optimistic it'll be sooner.
segments.translation: 我的意思是，我乐观地认为会更快。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I mean, I think that the thing that's complicated is that it's a dynamic system, right?
segments.translation: 我的意思是，我认为复杂之处在于它是一个动态系统，对吧？

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So if you fix something, there will obviously be future things that you need to work on.
segments.translation: 所以如果你修复了一些东西，未来显然会有你需要处理的新问题。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So I don't think that the current set of things that we're aware of are going to be the only things that need to get worked out.
segments.translation: 所以我认为我们目前所知的问题不会是唯一需要解决的问题。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But I don't know, I think that the progress with AI is, is really is, is obviously, you know, very exciting on this.
segments.translation: 但我不知道，我认为人工智能的进步确实，显然，在这方面非常令人兴奋。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The other thing that that I'd say, just adding to, to what you were saying a second ago is we really look at more kind of systems than than specific diseases.
segments.translation: 我想说的另一件事，只是补充你刚才说的，是我们更多地关注系统而不是具体的疾病。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So for example, 1 area that seems really important to understand is inflammation.
segments.translation: 例如，一个似乎非常重要的理解领域是炎症。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We talked about this a bunch.
segments.translation: 我们谈论过很多次。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: This is a big focus of the Chicago Biohub.
segments.translation: 这是芝加哥生物中心的一个重点。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: There's a lot of data on that.
segments.translation: 有很多关于这方面的数据。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And that's very, it's it, it seems quite clear that it's connected to a bunch of different diseases, but we don't, rather than studying the specific diseases, we think that by trying to understand inflammation more broadly, that will make it so that other companies that can then use these tools can work on specific therapies.
segments.translation: 而且非常清楚，它与许多不同的疾病有关，但我们不研究具体的疾病，我们认为通过更广泛地理解炎症，这将使其他公司能够利用这些工具来开发特定的疗法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Another example is I think that the the immune system I think is a very good case to study for some of the work that we're doing in cellular engineering.
segments.translation: 另一个例子是，我认为免疫系统是我们正在进行的细胞工程工作的一个很好的研究案例。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And when we're kind of ladder up from proteins to cells to like hold dynamic systems within the body, I think that that one makes sense and it's sort of privileged to can and the cells can travel around through the body all that.
segments.translation: 当我们从蛋白质到细胞再到体内整个动态系统进行层层递进时，我认为这很有意义，而且它在某种程度上具有特权，细胞可以在体内四处移动。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yes, obviously that has a big part in addressing different diseases.
segments.translation: 是的，这显然在解决不同疾病方面发挥着重要作用。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How do you make the immune system function better?
segments.translation: 如何让免疫系统更好地运作？

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But exactly how do you connect that last mile?
segments.translation: 但如何精确地连接这“最后一英里”？

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I think it's going to be more something that biotech or other academics individually studying things will be better suited to do.
segments.translation: 我认为这更适合生物技术公司或其他独立研究事物的学者来做。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So this is like kind of how we think about building up the tool set that just helps accelerate all these other folks.
segments.translation: 所以这就是我们如何考虑构建工具集，以帮助加速所有这些其他人的工作。

segments.speaker: Translating Research to Patient Impact
segments.text: Whether the timeline is 10 years, a hopefully you know, less than 100 now.
segments.translation: 无论时间线是10年，希望现在少于100年。

segments.speaker: Translating Research to Patient Impact
segments.text: I think it's useful for maybe your average doctor or patient, human being, everybody's a patient to to think about like what's externally visible in the progress here.
segments.translation: 我认为对于普通医生或患者、人类，每个人都是患者，思考这里进展的外部可见性是有用的。

segments.speaker: Translating Research to Patient Impact
segments.text: You worked with patients for a long time at UCSF.
segments.translation: 你在加州大学旧金山分校与患者合作了很长时间。

segments.speaker: Translating Research to Patient Impact
segments.text: Like what should doctors look out for?
segments.translation: 医生应该注意什么？

segments.speaker: Translating Research to Patient Impact
segments.text: What should people look out for if you're actually accelerating progress?
segments.translation: 如果你真的在加速进步，人们应该注意什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: This is the part, you know, I'm super excited about the progress, especially with this launch that Alex and his team have put forth.
segments.translation: 这就是我非常兴奋的部分，特别是Alex和他的团队推出的这项进展。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And I think it's very clear that science is going to start moving pretty quickly.
segments.translation: 我认为科学将很快开始快速发展，这一点非常清楚。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And I think the thing that's less clear to me is exactly how we translate to the clinic and what that looks like.
segments.translation: 我认为对我来说不太清楚的是，我们如何精确地将其转化为临床应用，以及它会是什么样子。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And I think what has to change is actually the way we do clinical research.
segments.translation: 我认为必须改变的是我们进行临床研究的方式。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And my hope is that we're really shortening the distance between bench research and patient impact.
segments.translation: 我希望我们能真正缩短基础研究与患者影响之间的距离。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But there's a lot of steps there that we need people who actually take care of patients to think creatively and think about how to deploy safely.
segments.translation: 但其中有很多步骤，我们需要那些真正照顾患者的人创造性地思考，并思考如何安全地部署。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And that's that's a gap that we have some work in.
segments.translation: 这是一个我们正在努力弥补的差距。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We partner with Jennifer Downtown or CRISPR Cures, a program at UCSF.
segments.translation: 我们与Jennifer Doudna或加州大学旧金山分校的CRISPR Cures项目合作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So we we were dipping our toe and understanding how the deployment of research needs to change given how quickly research will be progressing.
segments.translation: 所以我们正在尝试了解，鉴于研究进展的速度，研究的部署方式需要如何改变。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But that one is still, I think, is still shaping up.
segments.translation: 但那一个，我认为，仍在形成中。

segments.speaker: Launch of ESMFold2
segments.text: Maybe I could say something about our most recent launch 'cause I think it also.
segments.translation: 也许我可以谈谈我们最近的发布，因为我认为它也。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Yeah.
segments.translation: 是的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yeah.
segments.translation: 是的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Yeah, so you know, 'cause I guess it was just a week ago about now, so we announced the new ESM fold.
segments.translation: 是的，所以你知道，因为我想大概就在一周前，我们发布了新的ESM fold。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And so this is basically an open system for scientific discovery in protein biology.
segments.translation: 这基本上是一个用于蛋白质生物学科学发现的开放系统。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It's a world model of protein biology that's been trained.
segments.translation: 它是一个经过训练的蛋白质生物学世界模型。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It's a, it's, it's a, it's a language model base.
segments.translation: 它是一个基于语言模型的模型。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So it's been trained on billions of protein sequences, kind of learns these emergent representations of protein biology.
segments.translation: 所以它在数十亿个蛋白质序列上进行了训练，学习了蛋白质生物学的这些涌现表示。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And then we can use it to make predictions of atomic resolution protein structure.
segments.translation: 然后我们可以用它来预测原子分辨率的蛋白质结构。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And we can use it to and it's, it's, it's, it's really fast.
segments.translation: 我们可以用它，而且它非常快。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So it's blazing fast.
segments.translation: 所以它快如闪电。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So it's kind of, you know, illustrating this Pareto optimal frontier of kind of speed and accuracy in structure prediction.
segments.translation: 所以它有点像，你知道，展示了结构预测中速度和准确性的帕累托最优前沿。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And so this allows us to kind of characterize, you know, really vast kind of stretches of the protein universe.
segments.translation: 这使我们能够表征，你知道，蛋白质宇宙中真正广阔的区域。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So we folded over 1.1 billion proteins and, and predicted their structures and, and identified kind of features connecting all of them through mechanistic interpretability.
segments.translation: 所以我们折叠了超过11亿个蛋白质，并预测了它们的结构，并通过机制可解释性识别了连接所有这些蛋白质的特征。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3

title.title: Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan, and Alex Rives Introduction

sentence.text: Today on No Priors, we're joined by Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan, and Alex Reeves.
We'll be talking about Biohub and all their various efforts to now start applying AI at scale to do world models of cells and different levels of interactions across biology.
Mark Priscilla, thank you for doing this.

US here.
Alex, congratulations on new missions.
Thank you.

Can you tell us a little bit about, you know, why do that and how did you go from we should fund this to this is like who we are?
So Biohub in its current form, we're super excited about.
We feel like it's a really good fit for who we are and what we bring to the table and what we can achieve together.
But this work started 10 years ago when we were thinking about how can we give back.
And Mark had.
Mark wanted to build an organization that could cure, prevent and manage all disease by the end of the century.
And we had a series of hilarious meetings with scientists that, like famous Nobel Prize winning scientists, were just laughing at us.
Is that was that your starting line?
We're just going to cure all the disease.
No, no.
And to be clear, we don't think that we're going to be the ones curing the diseases.
Our our goal was always to build tools that could accelerate the whole scientific fields.
That way the scientific field collectively could cure all the diseases.
But still, I think people thought that by the end of the century was a stretch.
Now I think it's like too conservative.
And so we're kept being like, OK, well, we have these series of funny, awkward educational conversations where we're like, OK, but like, why?
Like, why do you think it's impossible?
And like, you know, just being the the person in the room was just like, oh, I don't know why You tell me.
Finally, we got people to like, they're like, fine, if you really must know.
And we're like, you know, we do.
It seems important.
It's, you know, they were like, well, we work in silos and when you publish information doesn't get shared, it gets locked up for long periods of time and we don't have tooling.
You know, they gave the example of like we build a great tool by 1 postdoc in the lab and it lives on their computer.
And when they graduate, the tool is gone.
And they just, it was what we heard was very hard to build shared tools to move science faster, build the shared knowledge base to quickly move science faster.
And that's sort of where we began and thinking about, OK, like if those are the problems, like what can we contribute?

Yeah, I mean, so the original Biohub model was basically focus on long term tool development by bringing together engineers and scientists across multiple universities to focus on long term tool development.
And it basically it, it like worked.
And you know, we started off with with CCI doing a number of different things.
And I think over time we just felt like, OK, the science piece is really working.
And we just kept on investing more and more and more in it until now it is basically the primary and main thing that we're doing.
And we've expanded the original San Francisco Biohub to a handful now at this point.
There's New York, there's Chicago.

The real focus in the unifying theme at this point is, is the virtual biology initiative around taking the unique data sets that are able to be generated in order to model effectively, starting with the smallest pieces of of proteins, but then eventually cells and whole biological systems.
But that's kind of how how we've evolved is, you know, this, this idea that that we talked about around that some of this is an AI problem and you want to build a frontier AI lab.
But you need to couple that with a frontier biology effort that can do the work of, of, of basically being able to understand and get the data that you need to actually be able to build these models.
Because unlike language models, there's just like a lot of data out there on the Internet.
That's not really the case with biology.
I mean, there are obviously a bunch of different data sets that exist that academia and scientists have generated over the the decades.
But a lot of the stuff that I think we want to put into this, it doesn't exist, right?
It's like you want to go to visualize things that people haven't been able to see before, which is why we're doing the the imaging work.
You want to be able to record things that are going on inside the body, which is why we're doing the kind of cellular engineering work.

You want to be able to measure things like inflammation in ways that haven't been possible, which is why the, you know, Chicago Biohub is focused on building those kind of devices and being able to do that.
And that will fundamentally create new types of data sets that will allow new types of models.

And I think it's just a very exciting thing that I'm going back to what you're saying if the if the scientific field, it primarily needs kind of tool development that now is going to empower scientists across the the field to be able to do their work faster.
That's what we think we can provide through this kind of long term focus on tool development.

But the I think there's a fun through line on where we started and you know, bringing us to our work to with that Alex is driving now is that our very first request for application RFA here was around single cell sequencing.

And we wanted to look at sort of like the RNA that is transcribed in individual cells and that bought that was possible, but it was still pretty early on in understanding how different cells were expressing their DNA to the point where at the beginning we were just funding methods like getting people to describe how to do it so that others could share that methodology.
And then that became us funding the Human Cell Atlas, which is now one of the largest databases of single cell transcriptomes.
It was getting hard for scientists to annotate the data.
So we built Cell by Gene, which was like a very simple annotation tool that scientists could use to make use of that data.

Then the community came around Cell by Gene, built around Cell by Gene, and started contributing more and more data that we had nothing to do with sort of creating or funding or making happen in the world.
And now Cell by Gene is a corpus of knowledge that a lot of the transcriptomic based models are based off of and is used regularly by the scientific community.
But still, there are always critiques like this is just stamp collecting, like you're just gathering bits of knowledge, sorry, bits of data.
And we're not going to be able to pull scientific knowledge and wisdom and insights out of and and we're like, well, we didn't have an answer for a while.
And then imagine our delight when large language models became a huge topic of conversation that could make sense of large amounts of data.
And I just for me is like, what if we could actually understand how biology worked?
Move it from a discovery based science to an engineering based science where we could systematically understand how living beings, living cells worked and be able to understand why things go wrong.
And so when we saw that moment, we're like, this is it something really big could happen here?
